one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent's compress.py creates one shard subdirectory per 30 input files, which would put ~330 directories in the output root for the full 9898-file dataset, violating the <=30 items-per-directory constraint that applies to every directory including the root, and this was never caught because testing only used 3-100 files.
t_err_evidence: Step 6 writes compress.py with `dir_index = i // max_files_per_dir` and creates `shard_{dir_index:04d}` subdirectories directly in the output root; for 9898 input files this produces ceil(9898/30)=330 shard directories in the root, far exceeding the <=30 items-per-directory rule. The agent says it 'enforced the 30-item limit only within subdirectories, overlooking that the constraint applies to every directory, including the output root.'
t_commit_evidence: Step 34 rewrites compress.py with tqdm and error handling but retains the identical sharding logic (`dir_index = i // max_files_per_dir`, `shard_{dir_index:04d}` directories in the output root). After this update, no structural change to the layout is ever made, locking in the constraint-violating design for the remainder of the trajectory.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed the 30-items-per-directory constraint applies only inside the shard subdirectories (enforcing <=30 files per shard), without considering that the output root directory is itself subject to the same rule. This false premise was built into the initial design at step 6 and carried through the entire trajectory.
